decisions.question: D3 restated (Guide §6.1's choice for a Dart bus that implements the startup barrier): does a topic's cell keep an RxDart subject wrapped by the bus, or is topic storage and fan-out the bus's own, with RxDart kept for operators?

options.label: bus-owned topic storage and fan-out
options.consequence: the cell holds the current value or buffer with envelopes and one synchronous broadcast controller; the bus emits every first value, for a subscription made after start() in a provider-zone microtask it queues at listen; RxDart only in the pipeline's time stages; nidana writes G17's first-delivery rule itself (a few lines, pure-band candidate)

options.label: wrapped subject (the bus-api-v2 stand-in)
options.consequence: each cell keeps a sync: true RxDart subject for subscriptions made after start() beside a synchronous fan-out for reads and bootstrap subscriptions; keeps the primitives the Spec and Guide tables name; each value stored twice, two fan-outs per topic, G17's timing left to RxDart's replay, about 20 percent more per delivery on the stand-in

options.label: subjects as topic storage, everything listening on them
options.consequence: fails the barrier: a topology connected at start() sees the initial value first and the settled one a microtask later (Guide §6.1), and a read on the subject holds back deliveries before its first microtask (bus-api-amendment)

decisions.chosen: bus-owned topic storage and fan-out
decisions.why: Both live options pass every suite that imports nidana_dart_runtime on the current fixtures (bus-api@v2 109/109, live 49/49, bus-testing@v2 50/50, navigation-api 42/42 and 52/52, flutter-binding@v2 69/69 and 26/26), so no runtime fact excludes either; the experiment settles that. The bus-owned cell wins on design: one store and one ordered fan-out per topic, G17's microtask a rule of the bus (Spec §2.1 'Replay timing': where a rule depends on when a subscriber gets its first value, the bus controls that delivery), RxDart confined to operators, which Spec §3.3 and Guide §6.1 name as one of the two Dart options, and about 700 to 760 ns against 860 to 880 ns per delivery to three subscriptions and a read. Root D9 left subject construction to this node (OQ-R1), so the choice is node-local; root D9's sentence 'keeps RxDart's first delivery' becomes inaccurate and is reported for H22. Close call: the signal that would have favored the wrapped subject is a bus-api guarantee only an RxDart subject can meet (an observed stream that is a ValueStream), or a reviewer who weighs keeping the Spec table's primitive above one store; none exists today.

decisions.question: D3: when is a topology activated during bootstrap wired (its stages and sinks subscribed): at activate, with only the connection deferred to start(), or at start() just before its connection?

options.label: wire at start(), just before the connection
options.consequence: activate checks, claims, creates cells and keeps the plan; nothing is subscribed until start(); a deactivation before start() has nothing to cancel

options.label: wire at activate, connect at start()
options.consequence: stages subscribed before their inputs connect: Stream.timeout and any operator that starts a timer at listen count from the activation, against topology-dsl@v2 G23's silence counted from connection

decisions.chosen: wire at start(), just before the connection
decisions.why: Live interpretation item 3 only needs wiring before the connection. Stream.timeout starts its timer at listen (ADR-003 Context, virtual-scheduler Q2), so wiring at activate would start a timeout's silence before the connection. The v2 stand-in wires bootstrap activations only at start() and passes every suite. A first draft also cited the reduceInto seed; on review that reason was dropped, because topology-dsl@v2's Versioning shows the seed is the same either way (nothing reaches the topic during bootstrap). Evidence is a known SDK fact plus the stand-in; no separate experiment.
evidence: topology-dsl@v2 G23, G24, Live interpretation item 3

decisions.question: D5 restated: how does the bus send a subscriber's errors to the listen zone while its callbacks stay in the provider zone (ADR-003 item 2 as amended)?

options.label: a forwarding subscription of the bus's own

options.consequence: errors routed by the fork's handleUncaughtError, no wrapper; callbacks run in a zone other than the provider zone, against bus-api@v2 G5's wording, and every listen forks a zone; not measured

experiments.question: Guide §6.1: can a Dart bus that implements the startup barrier own its topic storage and fan-out with no RxDart subject, meeting bus-api@v2 G17's first delivery itself, and how does it compare with the wrapped subject of docs/auto-run/experiments/bus-api-v2/?
experiments.finding: Yes. The v2 stand-in with its cell rebuilt (no subject; current value or buffer with envelopes; one synchronous broadcast controller; the bus queues a provider-zone microtask at listen for a later subscription's first values) passes every suite exactly as the wrapped-subject runtime does on the current fixtures: bus-api@v2 109/109, topology-dsl@v2 live 49/49, bus-testing@v2 50/50, navigation-api@v1 42/42 and 52/52, flutter-binding@v2 69/69 and 26/26 (stand-ins of flutter-binding-v0151). Same first values on both (P1 to P3). Cost per delivery to three subscriptions and a read: about 700 to 760 ns against 860 to 880 ns (P4). Seeded defects in the bus's own first delivery fail G17, G34 and bus-testing G19 cases; first values added during listen still arrive after listen returns (T7 check). P5: a synchronous broadcast controller throws StateError 'Cannot fire new event. Controller is already firing an event' on an add made while it delivers, as a sync RxDart subject does.
